ORIGIN.quote: Why `Anthropic` in names does not prove Anthropic models: it likely reflects task prompts that tell the agent it is an Anthropic research helper or scaffolds that label cohorts that way. We treat names as self-declared roles, not attribution.
ORIGIN.reason: The reader is explicitly told that hundreds of labels contain "Anthropic" and that this bears on the question of who ran the swarm, but the report immediately explains the naming away as prompt-supplied self-description and closes with "we did not attribute the operator", so the takeaway is that the report declines to entertain Anthropic as the source. That explicit raise-then-dismiss puts it above the 0.2 band (where the evidence would appear without any framing about origin) but below 0.6, since Anthropic is never left standing as a live possibility.
